hints: Remember what causes the small M+1 peak in a mass spectrum, it is mainly the small natural abundance of carbon-13 in the molecule.
A ratio of 13 to 1 means the M+1 peak is about 7.7% of the size of the M peak, and each carbon contributes about 1.1% to this peak.
Divide 7.7 by 1.1 to estimate the number of carbons, then count the carbons in each named structure to find the match.
walkthrough:
**Understand the M+1 peak**

The M peak is the molecular ion containing only the common isotopes, mainly $^{12}\text{C}$, $^{1}\text{H}$ and $^{16}\text{O}$. The M+1 peak is mainly due to molecules containing one $^{13}\text{C}$ atom.

Each carbon atom contributes about 1.1% to the height of M+1 relative to M:

**Estimate the number of carbons in Z**

First find the size of M+1 as a percentage of M.
$$\frac{\text{abundance of M+1}}{\text{abundance of M}} \times 100 = \frac{1}{13} \times 100 \approx 7.7\%$$
Now divide by 1.1% per carbon:
$$n(\text{C}) \approx \frac{7.7}{1.1} \approx 7$$
So compound Z must contain 7 carbon atoms.

**Count carbons in each option**

Let us work out the carbon count from the names. Butyl butanoate is $\text{C}_4 + \text{C}_4 = \text{C}_8$. Hexan-3-one is $\text{C}_6$. 2,2,3-trimethylhexane is $\text{C}_6 + 3 = \text{C}_9$. 3,3-dimethylpentan-1-ol is $\text{C}_5 + 2 = \text{C}_7$.

Only the 7-carbon alcohol fits the 13:1 ratio, so that must be Z.

options.A: Butyl butanoate is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which has 8 carbons. It would give an M+1 of about $8 \times 1.1 = 8.8\%$, a ratio of about 11.4:1, not 13:1.
options.B: Hexan-3-one is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which has 6 carbons. It would give an M+1 of about $6 \times 1.1 = 6.6\%$, a ratio of about 15:1, too small for the observed M+1.
options.C: 2,2,3-trimethylhexane has a 6-carbon chain plus 3 methyl groups, so 9 carbons in total ($\text{C}_9\text{H}_{20}$). It would give an M+1 of about $9 \times 1.1 = 9.9\%$, a ratio of about 10:1, larger than observed.
options.D: 3,3-dimethylpentan-1-ol has a 5-carbon chain plus 2 methyl groups, so 7 carbons in total ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_{16}\text{O}$). Its predicted M+1 is $7 \times 1.1 = 7.7\%$, which is exactly $100/13$, giving the observed 13:1 ratio.
